ranked.headline: New reference genomes and clade databases for seep tubeworms, seaweeds, planarians, corals
ranked.summary: Two de novo assemblies (tubeworm, red seaweed) appear alongside NAR database releases for planarians and stony corals, expanding non-model genomic infrastructure.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is genomic infrastructure for non-model eukaryotes, mostly marine. Two preprints report primary de novo assemblies. The first is a draft genome of the seep tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma, assembled and annotated from Oxford Nanopore and Illumina data. At 665 Mb in 6,320 scaffolds, it is draft rather than chromosome-level. The second is a reference genome for the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis, which ranges from saline NE Atlantic waters into the brackish Baltic. That distribution makes the genome relevant to salinity adaptation. Two NAR database papers work at the clade level. PlanMine 4.0 adds new planarian genomes, 70 flatworm transcriptomes and expanded expression resources. CoralDB integrates functional and evolutionary multi-omics data for stony corals, which are reef foundation species with little integrative multi-omics characterization. Together, these releases pair single-species references with curated, queryable platforms. That supports comparative and evolutionary genomics in taxa that lack mature model-organism resources.

ranked.headline: Joint modeling of variant classes, phenotypes and tissues sharpens gene-level inference
ranked.summary: Kernel tests, phenotype rescaling and multi-tissue eQTL or single-cell prioritization all move beyond marginal single-variant association toward gene-level evidence.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is association inference that jointly models heterogeneous variant classes, phenotypes or functional layers rather than relying on marginal single-variant tests. PrediXSKAT embeds PrediXcan-predicted expression into the SKAT kernel, testing rare coding and common cis-regulatory variants together to improve gene-level power. GiMat extends multivariate kernel regression to test SNP gene-gene interactions across multiple dichotomous phenotypes. SIQReg revisits an upstream choice usually left fixed, learning a phenotype scale transformation that minimizes quantile heterogeneity and improves GWAS, TWAS and polygenic prediction in UK Biobank. A second strand targets post-GWAS effector-gene prioritization at type 2 diabetes loci. CAS-X integrates fine-mapped eQTL PIPs and allelic fold changes across five metabolic tissues. CELL-X combines fine-mapped T2D genes with single-cell islet atlas data in an out-of-memory framework to prioritize beta-cell-relevant genes by cell type and disease state. SIQReg and GiMat are published; the other three remain preprints.

ranked.headline: Curated biomedical knowledgebases add machine-learning layers and programmatic access
ranked.summary: NAR database-issue updates (canSAR, CIViC, DGIdb, HIPPIE, FusionGDB, PRGdb) land together, pairing expanded curated content with predictive and interoperable tooling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is mature curated resources expanding coverage while adding predictive or machine-facing layers. canSAR 2026 integrates ML predictors, druggability tools and agentic-AI protein tools. CIViC 2026 introduces Feature entities, Molecular Profiles, AI-guided curation and ClinVar submission. PRGdb 5.0 grows to 874,967 candidate plant resistance proteins with DREM deep-learning prioritization. HIPPIE 3.0 reaches about 1.2M experimentally supported human PPIs and adds negative training sets aimed at interaction prediction. Interoperability and reproducibility form a second axis: DGIdb adds new sources, Python/R clients, Docker images and versioned releases. FusionGDB 3.0 covers 156K fusion genes from RNA-seq and WGS breakpoints and generates personalized fusion protein sequences. CiliaHub provides an expert-curated catalogue of over 2,500 ciliary genes with ClinVar variants. The IDKG preprint takes a graph-integration route, combining 20 infectious-disease sources into a Neo4j graph (4.6M nodes, 26M edges) for graph-based reasoning. Not every resource adds AI components.

ranked.headline: Curated references and portable tools sharpen microbial profiling and genome workflows
ranked.summary: An updated mOTUs-db, species-level 16S resources, and browser-native and Nextflow tooling target interoperable microbial and comparative genomics analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is improving microbial taxonomic profiling through curated reference data and interoperable tooling. The mOTUs-db update links taxonomy to genome-encoded function and environmental and geographic distributions, with a CLI and API for profiling. RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies sequenced variable regions, to support species-level identification. VPHYL, an R Shiny app, converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore 16S abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects with automated HTML reports. Sparrowhawk adds a deployment angle: a WebAssembly framework for browser-based tools that run locally, keeping data private, demonstrated with lightweight microbial genomics methods. On the genome side, nf-core/pairgenomealign wraps LAST pairwise whole-genome alignment in a scalable Nextflow pipeline with benchmarking, and ABAQS scores annotation quality via completeness, gene model validity and protein profile accuracy across over 1700 fungal genomes. Scopes differ; no cross-tool performance comparisons are supported.

ranked.headline: Tumour single-cell and spatial transcriptomics consolidate into queryable public resources
ranked.summary: TISCH3, a 42-cancer TME atlas and PDAC BioPortal expand tumour single-cell and spatial resources, while new methods add spatial context and multimodal fusion.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the consolidation of tumour transcriptomic data into public, queryable resources, with spatial data increasingly built into the analysis layer. TISCH3 grows to 477 datasets, adding 218 scRNA-seq and 69 spatial transcriptomics collections with spatial analysis tools. A pan-cancer single-cell screen across 42 cancers reports tumour microenvironment programs conserved across organs and species, and releases an atlas with scTME software. PDAC BioPortal combines bulk, single-nucleus and spatial pancreatic cohorts with pathway and survival tools. DriverDBv5 and X-BCRdb extend the resource layer to multi-omics driver genes and BCR-paired single-cell clonotype–transcriptome data. Methods target analytical gaps. SpaceMACE adds spatial information to tumour-cell annotation alongside CNV inference, and HIT-Fuse applies hierarchical tensor fusion to six omics and pathomics modalities while handling missing modalities. A Cell Reports study on genomic burden and selection in genetic immune escape across cancers is related but less directly tied to resource building.

ranked.headline: Regulatory state is increasingly read out and predicted at cell-type resolution across modalities
ranked.summary: Preprints pair cell-type-conditioned prediction with single-cell, long-read and multi-omic readouts, tying regulatory state to cell identity in tissues and disease.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving regulatory state by cell type, with both predictive and experimental routes. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb DNA and provides an enhancer-gene link atlas. Experimental methods add measurement: TrES-seq pairs scRNA-seq with nanobody-Tn5 histone mark profiling, COMET assigns bulk long reads to cell types by methylation, and Superb-seq links Cas9 edits to single-cell transcriptomes. DRAFT infers dynamic regulatory networks from time-resolved multi-omics trajectories, and a pan-cancer lncRNA atlas links lncRNAs to regulons. Siphon-seq and the heart isoform atlas extend this to purity-aware platelet profiling and full-length isoforms. What is new is the coupling of perturbation, epigenomic or isoform readouts to cell identity; these data could in principle test cell-type-conditioned predictors, though no item does so directly.

ranked.headline: Reference-free interface scoring and low-distortion mapping extend geometric analysis of protein-protein interfaces
ranked.summary: MDQ and TopoPPI offer new ways to score and visualize protein-protein interfaces, alongside work on coarse-grained models and ensemble generation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative geometric treatment of protein-protein interfaces. MDQ is a symmetric, reference-free, DockQ-inspired score that compares interfaces across molecular dynamics frames and yields a distance metric for clustering. TopoPPI, the one published article, extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty to map interfaces into low-distortion 2D atlases for visualization. The new element is interface comparison without a reference structure, and contact-weighted geometric mapping. The remaining preprints are structurally related but do not share this focus: they cover topological chunking for simulated-annealing sequence design, coarse-graining choices in machine-learned protein models, IDP ensemble generation from sequence-derived geometric priors, and AlphaFold-supported analysis of NCF1. Their outputs and benchmarks differ, so results are not directly comparable.

ranked.headline: Cross-cohort and cross-platform evaluation frames claims in omics and tabular biomedical prediction
ranked.summary: Five preprints pair new predictors with cross-platform, benchmark or external-cohort tests, while one reports a single 184-patient cohort.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how evaluation design bounds what a biomedical predictive claim supports. PRTS predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes preprocessing over 94 public tabular datasets and compares 23 models; foundation models lead, but tree-based methods remain competitive. SNOWS tests transfer to CGGA, raising C-index from 0.691 to 0.712. SOSM reports a C-index of 0.768 on a single 184-patient ccRCC cohort, a narrower evidence base. Elflow is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. The new element is a shift toward cross-platform, external-cohort and standardized comparison. These items do not establish whether curated public benchmarks reflect generalization under deployment conditions.

ranked.headline: Causal discovery methods are benchmarked under latent confounding and perturbation data
ranked.summary: New benchmarks test temporal and interventional causal discovery on kinetic models and CRISPR data, exposing method limits under partial observability.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is head-to-head evaluation of existing causal discovery methods on biological networks. A bioRxiv preprint compares temporal approaches (tMIIC, PCMCI+/LPCMCI, SVAR-FCI) on simulated biochemical kinetic models, with fully and partially observed settings that include latent confounders and unobserved variables. A published study compares interventional causal structure learning algorithms on synthetic and CRISPR perturbation data for gene regulatory network inference. The emphasis is on assessing methods under partial observability and with interventional data rather than proposing new algorithms. Two further items, hierarchical dynamical surrogates of trust-game decisions and ODE-based reconstruction of hidden epidemic states with multi-agent reinforcement learning, share a theme of inference from incomplete observations but do not address causal network benchmarking.

ranked.headline: Models predict unmeasured expression, protein and 3D gene fields from histology and sparse spatial data
ranked.summary: New preprints infer unmeasured RNA, protein and 3D expression from H&E, sliced spatial data and transcript geometry, alongside perturbation and embedding methods.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting molecular readouts that were not directly assayed. SCOPE predicts single-cell RNA and protein levels from H&E using RNA-protein biomarker priors, reporting improved Pearson correlation across 16 organs. HoloGene lifts pre-registered spatial slices into continuous 3D gene-expression fields with an anisotropic conditional implicit neural representation. A rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds and improves protein prediction. scPACE imputes missing cell states in cohort data. A second strand concerns perturbation and signaling: OCCAM predicts perturbation effects, and CIRCE infers graded signaling activity from combinatorial perturbation structure. Representation work includes scUNVEIL's next-UMI pretraining on about 92M cells, GatorAnchor's uncertainty-aware neighborhoods, and CIRCA's identifiable cell and niche programs. Spatial multi-omic modeling (multiCAsp) and domain detection (CASTLE) are adjacent rather than inference-focused.

ranked.headline: Clinical ML evaluation exposes limits of AUC, same-platform validation and uncalibrated confidence
ranked.summary: Three preprints show headline discrimination metrics can hide timing insensitivity, weak uncertainty calibration and near-chance cross-platform transfer.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is evaluation rather than architecture. The mammography study reports that AUC and C-index for breast cancer risk models are insensitive to diagnosis timing, and proposes a two-stage whether-versus-when model. CALIFUSE fuses several frozen pathology foundation models and uses representational disagreement and Jensen-Shannon chunk agreement to obtain calibrated uncertainty in whole-slide image classification. The glioblastoma circulating miRNA study tests CTGAN and TVAE augmentation and finds that same-modality validation overstates performance, with cross-platform AUROC around 0.40-0.47, near chance. Together they point to timing, calibration and cross-platform transfer as properties that standard discrimination metrics do not capture. All three are preprints, so the findings are provisional.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks calibrate long-read pipelines for SVs, isoforms and m6A, alongside signal-level assembly
ranked.summary: New benchmarks of local assembly, Kinnex RNA-seq and Dorado m6A calling define when long-read variant and modification calls are reliable.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation and calibration of long-read analysis. A preprint compares five local-assembly consensus strategies for SV calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data and reports data-type-dependent performance. A Genome Medicine study tests PacBio Kinnex RNA-seq against short-read sequencing for Mendelian diagnosis in 50 individuals, with a new isoform pipeline. An eLife study benchmarks Dorado versions for direct-RNA m6A against GLORI and proposes stringent filtering and a best-practice workflow. HARICOT, which assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling, is a distinct methodological direction. GapCNV, TERRACE 2.0 and the Drosophila transposon-isoform study concern CNV detection, circular RNA assembly and isoform diversity, and are adjacent to the long-read work. The items do not show joint variant and modification calling.

ranked.headline: Explicit network, ODE, Bayesian and causal models are used to infer regulatory structure from expression data
ranked.summary: New preprints and papers pair explicit model structure with expression data to infer feedback, transcription kinetics, copy number and spatial causality.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit model structure to extract regulatory or causal organization from expression measurements. Three preprints illustrate this: a systematic analysis of gene network topologies identifies feedback loops as drivers of restored heterogeneity from homogeneous populations; a semi-mechanistic ODE transcription model of zebrafish maternal-to-zygotic transition is fitted to RNA-seq to define expression clusters; and causal-discovery algorithms applied to Visium liver data model local and neighbor-derived effects in senescence. Echidna adds a Bayesian hierarchical model integrating scRNA-seq with bulk WGS to infer copy number alterations across samples and treatment time points. A 161-method cell-cell communication review, the LACA and CellStressDB resources, and a Shapley-explained chromatin imaging study are related context rather than mechanistic expression models.

ranked.headline: Ground-truth simulation, fast relatedness inference and unified references support comparative genomics
ranked.summary: New tools supply simulated ground truth, scalable ancient DNA relatedness screening and a unified ERV reference for validating comparative inference.
ranked.synthesis: The items address different problems, so the common thread is infrastructure for evaluating and scaling evolutionary inference rather than a shared algorithm. OrthoSimulator generates empirically calibrated simulated datasets with known orthogroups and gene trees, giving ground truth for benchmarking orthology inference. fastpmr is a memory-efficient pairwise mismatch-rate method for relatedness inference, reported as over 1000x faster than READv2, and is applied to screen the global ancient DNA record. ERV Navigator integrates human endogenous retrovirus annotations, nomenclatures and genomic loci into one phylogenetically informed reference database. What is new is the pairing of explicit truth or reference frameworks with tooling that scales, which makes comparative inference easier to validate and to apply to larger datasets.

ranked.headline: EEG decoding is tested for transfer across subjects, stimuli and deployment, with controls exposing spurious accuracy
ranked.summary: New preprints stress cross-subject transfer, adaptation cost and sham controls, showing decoding accuracy may not hold beyond the conditions where it was measured.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether EEG and neural decoding performance holds outside the conditions in which it was measured. ReBrain transfers an intracranial EEG prior to scalp signals without paired data or fine-tuning, and AMRT reports cross-subject generalization for continuous motor decoding. The BCI study frames adapting frozen EEG encoders as a resource-priced decision using gated Bayesian heads. The EEG-video study is most explicit on validity: contrastive alignment beats CCA for seen stimuli but not novel videos, and a sham control shows accuracy can be spurious. NeuroSim adds a simulator with injected disease biomarkers for classifier development. What is new is the emphasis on transfer, adaptation cost and negative controls. None of the items tests a causal or mechanistic account, so mechanistic validity remains open.

ranked.headline: Protein models are probed for evolutionary signal, structural fidelity and use in phylogenetic analysis
ranked.summary: New work scrutinizes what AlphaFold and protein foundation models encode about evolution and structure, alongside a web tool for protein evolutionary characterization.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how well protein structure and sequence models capture evolutionary information and biological reality. AlphaInterp applies mechanistic interpretability to AlphaFold 3, reporting that a few divergent MSA homologues suffice to recover structure, via pairformer latent geometry and confidence outputs. A study of experimentally validated non-globular proteins shows where AlphaFold predictions diverge from biologically relevant structural states. A review of transformer protein foundation models covers residue dependencies, pathogenicity and alignment-free evolutionary analysis. MolEvolvR complements these with a web app that combines domain-centric searches, phylogenies and domain architecture across superkingdoms. What is new is the emphasis on dissecting what these models encode and where they fail, paired with accessible tools for evolutionary characterization.

ranked.headline: Standardised annotation tools and population-specific databases extend genomic analysis reach
ranked.summary: New HLA annotation, Indian variant, national database and 1000 Genomes hash resources broaden access to structured, reusable genomic data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is reusable genomic infrastructure that turns variant-level data into structured resources for downstream analysis. hlafactor, a C++20 tool, standardises multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation (tapasin dependency, expression, NK ligand groups) from two-field genotypes. GI-DB addresses underrepresentation of the Indian population in global genomic resources with a variant database reflecting its ethnolinguistic and biogeographical diversity. The CNCB-NGDC 2027 update adds thirteen new resources spanning genome variation and health and disease, among others. A preprint releases a public dataset of haploblock-based genomic hashes and clusters for 2,548 1000 Genomes individuals, generated with an optimized Genomic Cluster Engine pipeline for etiological subtyping. The items are heterogeneous in purpose; the shared novelty is expanded, standardised access rather than a single method.

ranked.headline: Sequence- and descriptor-based models target binding, kinetics, turnover and molecular properties
ranked.summary: Five reports tailor architectures to binding affinity, Koff, kcat-like turnover and property prediction without explicit complex structures.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is architecture design for predicting protein-ligand and related molecular quantities from learned representations of sequences, fingerprints and graphs, not from explicit complex geometry. STORM is presented as a lightweight structure-free binding affinity model. MGCA combines ESM2 and Morgan fingerprints in a multi-granularity cross-attention mixture-of-experts for dissociation kinetics (Koff). EnzRef adapts frozen protein language models with reference-centered cross-attention and role-aware recomposition of reactant/product conditions for enzyme turnover. ReMoD-Mol (modality weighting plus descriptor-guided distillation) and ontology pre-training for metabolites extend the representation question to property prediction. The summaries give no validation protocols or benchmark diagnostics beyond ReMoD-Mol's comparison with 14 baselines, so evidence on generalization and scoring reliability remains limited.

ranked.headline: Computational analysis of RNA sequence and structure across genomes, pathogens and expression systems
ranked.summary: Comparative motif screens and an S. aureus sRNA atlas sit beside studies of RNA folding in host mRNA partitioning and 5' UTR-mediated translation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational analysis of RNA sequence and structure, applied to genomes, transcriptomes and design problems. Two preprints apply comparative and integrative methods. A CMfinder and R-scape screen identifies seven candidate structured ncRNA motifs across protist genomes. aureoRNA integrates phylogeny, public transcriptomes and computational predictions into an interactive atlas of S. aureus sRNAs and their targets. The published items are less directly about ncRNA discovery. A Cell study reports that RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates. A Bioinformatics study models how promoter choice alters 5' UTR-mediated translation in E. coli and introduces the web service UTR Designer Pro. Preprint findings remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Brain cell-type molecular atlases are paired with tools linking them to disease, development and connectivity
ranked.summary: Curated atlases and web tools now tie brain cell-type expression to disease, development, spatial and connectome context across mouse and human datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure that makes cell-type-resolved brain molecular data reusable and interpretable in context. Resource work includes harmonized sample metadata for wild-type and Alzheimer's disease model mouse sc/snRNA-seq, a multi-omic QTL atlas from 231 human prefrontal cortex donors connecting disorder risk to cell-type and developmental regulation, and scCVD, which spans 701 samples and over 4.68 million cells with scRNA-seq and ATAC-seq for cerebrovascular disease. Tools extend interpretation to other layers: SCOUBI uses a neural network to map axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in mouse spatial transcriptomics, VEGABrain projects bulk RNA-seq onto developing human brain atlas surfaces with precomputed ssGSEA maps, and CSDX links human expression to mouse connectome strength. Species, tissue and modality vary across these works.

ranked.headline: Latent models link histology, spatial transcriptomics and single-cell states
ranked.summary: Histology-to-molecule foundation models and 3D atlas methods now couple morphology with spatial and single-cell omics readouts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is structured latent representation of spatial and single-cell omics, with several items linking morphology to molecular readouts. Loki2 recovers transcriptomic and protein signals and morphology-linked latents from H&E images, GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology, and sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphology features to spatial transcriptomics. Space-map aligns serial sections into 3D single-cell atlases, and SOUR separates heritable lineage from microenvironmental effects on tumor gene expression. Statistical assessment is a shared emphasis: velotest quantifies RNA velocity embedding fidelity, and MiSA tests spatial dysbiosis. TMCells and the hybrid mixture model offer non-spatial probabilistic alternatives.

ranked.headline: Interpretable ML for peptide ADMET and simulated binding training data
ranked.summary: Simulated peptide binding data and site-level attributions aim to make ADMET models inspectable before candidate ranking.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning for peptide and macrocycle pharmacology, with ADMET prediction as the central endpoint. AIO applies an interpretable multimodal framework to cyclic peptides and macrocycles, using solvent-aware contrastive pretraining. VReceptor simulates sequence-dependent peptide binding data through pharmacophore-inspired weighting, offering a route to training data for such models. PTM-BDL extends the interpretability concern to post-translational modification states, linking typed PTM states with sequence, structure and drug features to predict drug response (IC50, resistance), with site-level integrated-gradients attributions. ADCdb 2.0 is a reference resource rather than a model, compiling ADMET profiles for 542 antibody-drug conjugates alongside clinical and bioactivity data. What is new is the pairing of simulated training data with attribution at individual sites, which makes model behaviour inspectable before candidates are ranked.

ranked.headline: Latent haplotypes, linkage structure and unsampled phylogeny regions made explicit
ranked.summary: Preprints now treat haplotypes, linkage disequilibrium and unsampled phylogeny regions as explicit latent targets.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread in this set is replacing a simplifying step with an explicit formulation of an unobserved quantity. DiGi treats diploid genotyping on a pangenome haplotype trellis graph as an exact integer program, jointly inferring two haplotype paths from reads. LDEN estimates whole-genome linkage disequilibrium from short-read viral sequencing data by alternating projections onto positive semidefinite matrices, so the target is fitted under explicit constraints. The third item applies machine learning and beam search to localize unsampled regions in partially sampled pathogen phylogenies from the observed tree alone; its connection to the first two is weaker. What is new is the target itself: haplotype configurations, genome-wide linkage structure and unsampled phylogenetic portions are each modeled as latent objects to be inferred.

ranked.headline: Nucleic acid foundation models are being tailored to specific biological constraints
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair sequence foundation models with task-specific design for regulatory, ncRNA, and lncRNA prediction tasks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is specialization: models are pretrained on or built for a narrow biological domain rather than reused as generic embeddings. GPN is pretrained on 455 apicomplexan assemblies and improves epigenomic prediction in Plasmodium falciparum. MARRI encodes hybridization physics directly, combining opening penalties and hybridization gains in cross-RNA attention on top of pretrained RNA representations. LncRFM supplies an open lncRNA pretraining corpus and evaluation suite and reports gains over RNA foundation models on lncRNA prediction, while B-RANKO unifies sequence generation and representation learning for ncRNA. The nitrogenase work and the coding-versus-intergenomic CNN address different sequence problems, so the shared thread is task specialization rather than a single architecture.

ranked.headline: Validation protocols expose what biological sequence models actually learn
ranked.summary: Headline accuracy is giving way to scrutiny of confounds, held-out splits and measured targets in protein and peptide predictors.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether predictive scores for biological sequences track the property of interest once confounds are controlled. The antimicrobial peptide protocol enforces homology separation and length matching, and finds that length alone separates classes. ProtCOVER applies family-level conformal calibration to variant effect predictors on unseen protein families, with density-ratio reweighting under descriptor shift. The ESMC interpretability benchmark tests protein language model internals against residue-level curated annotations, and its conclusions on depth, probes, neurons and SAEs depend on that validation setup. Match and Correct probes OpenFold's Evoformer layers for distance decodability and triangle-inequality violations. MADM and PhageLysClass extend architecture scope through PLM embeddings for developability and phage lytic protein classification. What is new is explicit scrutiny of what these models exploit and what they are validated against, rather than headline accuracy alone.

ranked.headline: Curated structure databases for RNA, protein-ligand and protein-peptide complexes
ranked.summary: Recent releases expand RNA, covalent ligand and peptide interaction resources with AlphaFold3 models and ML-oriented curation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure that organizes experimental and predicted 3D structural information for downstream modeling. RR3DD 2.0 expands RNA 3D structure classification to 15,764 chains, clustered by RMscore into 1,042 clusters and mapped to Rfam. CovPDB 2.0 grows to about 6200 covalent protein-ligand complexes and adds AlphaFold3 cofolding models with predicted cysteine ligandability. Propedia 26 updates a protein-peptide interaction database explicitly aimed at machine learning applications. RNAcomp2D differs in kind: it is a web tool that runs thermodynamic and deep learning secondary structure predictors and visually compares their outputs. The common emphasis is curated, structure-linked resources and comparison layers; the listed records do not show physics-based modeling itself, and benchmarking evidence is not given in the summaries.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved references reshape association and expression analysis
ranked.summary: Recent pig, Capsicum, apple and pedigree studies show haplotype-aware references changing downstream genetic and expression inference.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the replacement of a single linear reference with haplotype-resolved assemblies and pangenome graphs, and the propagation of that representation into downstream inference. In the apple study, a matched parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith genome changes RNA-seq differential expression and the biological conclusions drawn from it. The Capsicum workflow uses a graph pangenome to localize k-mer GWAS hits and link capsaicinoid and aroma traits to haplotypes and candidate loci. PolyOrigin2 addresses the upstream haplotype reconstruction step in multi-generational diploid and tetraploid pedigrees. The pig pan-genome, with three T2T and sixteen high-quality assemblies, extends this to centromere evolution, structural variation and genotype-phenotype mapping. The new element is the integration of haplotype-aware representation across reference construction, association testing and expression analysis, although the items occupy different stages of this pipeline.

ranked.headline: Core sequence, literature and omics databases report 2026–2027 infrastructure updates
ranked.summary: Public sequence, literature, and metabolomics resources report expanded scale and automated annotation or validation in 2026–2027 updates.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the upkeep of large public biological data resources, where content growth is paired with updates to submission, transfer, validation, and annotation infrastructure. The tRNAdb 2026 release extends a compilation of tRNA sequences and genes that originated as an extension of Sprinzl's seminal collection. Europe PMC's 2026 update reports 48M open abstracts with text-mined and new machine-learning annotations plus expanded identifier handling. MetaboLights describes 2027 developments including a submission workflow, Globus transfers, a validation framework, and dataset reuse support. INSDC reports that its global nucleotide archive now exceeds 75 PB, alongside new governance, a membership pathway, and planned AI-assisted metadata work. What is new is the explicit engineering of automated ingestion, validation, and machine-assisted annotation within resources of this scale. The items are heterogeneous, and the dominant thread applies most directly to the MetaboLights and Europe PMC entries.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale metabolic models are curated, extended, and paired with learned inference
ranked.summary: Four new preprints extend genome-scale reconstructions with curation, ME-model extensions, and learned flux and essentiality inference.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the construction and extension of genome-scale metabolic frameworks, increasingly coupled to data-driven inference. iJL1143 was built as a curated model of Fusarium venenatum A3/5 from an A. niger template and validated against batch fermentation biomass data. coralME v1.3 extends ME-model analysis to non-canonical amino acid translation, protein and RNA degradation reactions, arbitrary coupling coefficients, and cofactor essentiality in bacterial models. On the inference side, HyperGenie applies directed hypergraph neural networks to genome-scale models to predict bacterial gene essentiality from wild-type flux features, while Flux Transformer infers mass-balanced fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates. The new element is learned models operating directly on curated reconstructions and labeling data. This pattern describes the dominant thread across these four preprints rather than every item, since coralME is primarily a software extension.

ranked.headline: Open Python workflows assign bacterial genomes to species and transmission groups
ranked.summary: Pathogen-agnostic, reproducible tools now assign bacterial genomes to species and transmission groups from whole-genome data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is open, computationally accessible tooling that organizes bacterial genomes into standardized groups. Robust Cluster Typing applies a Snakemake/Python workflow that uses ribosomal proteins to assign genomes to species-level clusters, demonstrated on Campylobacter. SNP2Cluster-Py provides an open-source Python framework for context-aware core SNP clustering of pathogen isolates, tested on Klebsiella and pneumococcal whole-genome datasets. P2CS-Web is a different kind of contribution: an updated curated resource linking prokaryotic two-component system repertoires to domain architectures, genomic neighbourhoods and sequence clusters. The two preprints present analysis workflows, whereas P2CS-Web is a database update. What is new is the pathogen-agnostic, reproducible treatment of species designation and transmission-cluster analysis from whole-genome data, with ribosomal proteins as the basis for species assignment in the first item.

ranked.headline: Circuit structure links spiking dynamics to locomotor control and connectivity inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints examine how spiking circuit architecture governs locomotor rhythm and the inference of structural connectivity from activity.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that circuit dynamics depend on architecture and operating regime. The synchronization preprint introduces a composite metric for identifying antiphase locking in a biomorphic spiking CPG embedded in a neuromuscular loop. The Rat v2 preprint pairs a biomechanical rat body with Rat NCAP, a spinal-circuit-based neural architecture, and GPU training infrastructure for simulating rat locomotion. The third preprint reverses the direction of inference: an in silico study of spatially constrained modular spiking networks shows how spatial constraints and dynamical regime affect recovery of structural connectivity from simulated activity. What is new is the explicit link between architectural priors and locomotor control, and between regime dependence and structural inference. The items do not share a common method or system, so the connection rests on the architecture-dynamics relationship rather than on shared tooling.

ranked.headline: EPIC2: integrating single-cell chromatin accessibility with human genetics to identify trait-relevant cell types
ranked.summary: EPIC2 is an R framework that links GWAS summary statistics with single-cell chromatin accessibility, accounting for linkage disequilibrium, to rank…

ranked.headline: Deep learning de novo peptide sequencing extends to TMT-labeled and modified peptides
ranked.summary: Three 2026 preprints extend deep learning de novo sequencing to unlabeled spectra, TMTpro-labeled phosphopeptides, and integrated rescoring workflows.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational improvement of peptide identification from tandem mass spectra, pursued through model training and post-search processing. SemiNovo applies a semi-supervised framework that learns from unlabeled spectra using the DarkSpec corpus and mass-constrained modelling. Casanovo-TMT extends the Casanovo de novo model to TMTpro-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides, reporting 84.7% exact-peptidoform accuracy. MSGFLEX provides an end-to-end proteomics and metaproteomics pipeline built on MS-GF+, adding XPECTRA XGBoost rescoring and QUANTIX protein quantification, and is reported to outperform Percolator. What is new is the extension of deep learning sequencing to labeled and modified peptides and the integration of rescoring with quantification in one workflow. The items are heterogeneous in scope: SemiNovo concerns training data, while MSGFLEX concerns pipeline design and quantification.

ranked.headline: Ion identity and competition shape RNA, transporter, and ribosome structure
ranked.summary: Simulations now treat specific ion species and their competition as explicit structural determinants across condensates, transporters, and ribosomes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of molecular simulation to attribute structural and functional behavior to specific ion species and their coordination geometry. In the RNA condensate study, coarse-grained simulations link multidentate Mg2+ phosphate coordination to spatial ion gradients and heterogeneous organization within condensates. The XPR1 study, combining MD simulations over 110 µs with free-energy calculations, attributes H2PO4- over HPO4^2- selectivity to protein-phosphate interactions and direct ion-ion competition. Coarse-grained simulations of the bacterial 70S ribosome show that K+ versus Mg2+ identity alters flexibility and long-range coupling across the particle. What is new is the explicit treatment of ion identity and competition as determinants of structure, rather than ions as a uniform background. The systems differ, so the shared element is methodological and mechanistic rather than a common biological context.

ranked.headline: Quality checks and validation tools for LC-MS annotations and feature tables
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add retention-time validation and quality screening to LC-MS workflows, aiming for reliability before results are reused.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the downstream stage of mass spectrometry analysis, where annotations, feature tables and quantitative outputs are checked before they are interpreted or reused. LipidRT applies retention time coherence to validate and expand lipid annotations in untargeted reversed-phase LC-MS lipidomics. MetaboRx integrates quality metrics and preprocessing for LC-MS metabolomics feature tables, detecting formatting errors and unreliable features. OSMSS parses proteomics search outputs and runs guided differential abundance, phosphosite and enrichment analyses through a no-code Shiny interface. qPTM 3.0 consolidates fragmented quantitative PTM data into a knowledgebase for reuse. What is new is the explicit emphasis on quality checks and accessible Shiny front ends for non-coders. None of these items is presented as a new spectral identification algorithm.

ranked.headline: Stochastic gene regulatory models link network topology to cell differentiation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple stochastic GRN dynamics to differentiation landscapes, GPU-scale network optimization and topology-driven fate patterns.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is the use of explicit gene regulatory network models to link stochastic expression with cell-state heterogeneity and differentiation. The PDE-integral framework in arXiv:2611.19257 couples stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics with population renewal to define a dynamic Waddington landscape. The jaxgrn framework in arXiv:2611.20172 applies differentiable programming to optimize thousands of networks end-to-end on GPUs using stochastic simulation. The bioRxiv preprint 10.64898/2026.11.18.767571 works at the level of network topology, reporting that positive-cycle tangles and mutual inhibition enable hierarchical differentiation patterns in simulated dynamic GRN models. The novelty lies in the joint treatment of population-level renewal, landscape geometry, and large-scale network optimization. All three are unreviewed preprints, so these results remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Generative flow and bridge models capture single-cell state transitions
ranked.summary: Four recent preprints extend generative trajectory models to division, mass change, and perturbation response in single-cell and spatial data.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is learning generative dynamics that transport cell states over time, using flow matching or Schrödinger bridges as the core machinery. ST-FateFlow couples gene-expression and spatial velocity fields with a time-conditioned differentiation potential learned from time-resolved spatial transcriptomics. HORIZON applies flow matching to spatiotemporal cell dynamics and removes rigid frame motion before modeling. Elysium is a simulation-free unbalanced Schrödinger bridge solver that jointly learns state transitions and mass change. MitoWorld generates single-cell future images under gene knockdown by combining latent dynamics, a division hazard, and diffusion rendering. What is new across the set is explicit treatment of division, mass change, and perturbation response within generative trajectory frameworks.

ranked.headline: Graph and k-mer structures replace linear references in haplotype and ancestry inference
ranked.summary: Population-scale pangenome analysis reveals 531 novel TR germline alleles, while graph-aligned phasing extends haplotype assignment beyond linear references.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the move from linear-reference or variant-call inputs toward graph-based representations in genome analysis. GRASER phases graph-aligned short reads directly against individual haplotype paths, using unique graph edges to avoid linear-reference bias. A population-scale pangenome analysis of 232 individuals with the gAIRR Suite version 2 reports 531 novel TR germline alleles and 99.985% recall. Genomic tessellations introduce a canonical factorization of DNA into quasi-periodic tiles with a tessellated BWT index for faster long-read mapping. MitoArc provides a Nextflow workflow for short-read mtDNA analysis with circular-coordinate processing and NUMT-aware evaluation on synthetic truth data. Taken together, the new element is the use of graph structures for haplotype and germline inference at population scale; the tessellation and mtDNA items address less directly aligned problems.

ranked.headline: Fragment anchors and spectral language models advance metabolite annotation
ranked.summary: Untargeted metabolomics annotation is moving beyond whole-spectrum similarity toward fragment-level anchors and learned spectrum-to-function mapping.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extracting biological meaning from tandem mass spectra in untargeted metabolomics. ANCHor moves annotation beyond whole-spectrum similarity by using fragment anchors shared among similar spectra, and it is applied to untargeted metabolomics features. Spec2Function takes a complementary route, inferring biological functions directly from MS2 spectra with a dual-encoder contrastive model and retrieval-augmented generation. What is new is the coupling of contrastive spectrum representations with retrieval-augmented generation to link spectra to function, rather than to structural identity alone. SynCED, a published update of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database, is a reference resource for synthetic chemical exposure data. It is heterogeneous relative to the two preprints and is included as a database rather than as a modelling advance.

ranked.headline: Evolutionary search, sequence models, and structure prediction refine TF binding motifs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply evolutionary search, deep sequence models, and protein-DNA structure prediction to refine transcription factor motif discovery at scale.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints converge on transcription factor (TF) motif inference, each addressing a different aspect of how motifs are identified and interpreted. A MAP-Elites evolutionary approach with variable-length motif genotypes is validated against HOCOMOCO on five liver ChIP-seq datasets, with diversity preservation aimed at recovering motifs under challenging confounder landscapes. BPNet models trained on roughly 2,000 ENCODE TF binding profiles indicate that motif cooperativity contributes negligibly to genome-wide binding. ZebraMotif applies AlphaFold3 and NA-MPNN to model protein-DNA structures, yielding zebrafish motifs for 2,543 TFs. What is new is the source of motif evidence: evolutionary search, sequence-based modelling, and predicted protein-DNA structure.
